The preposition and the construct noun it stands before are rendered by the single English in, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the two share one unit, headed on the morpheme carrying the lexeme; this is rule 19's rider, and the chapter reads lipne as before (13.22) and al odot as because of (13.24) on the same terms, while al pi (13.3) and al yad (13.29) split only because each morpheme holds English of its own. The suffix is the rectum and keeps its own pronoun under rule 19. Competing reading, which BSB takes: in is the preposition's alone and tavekh is unrepresented under rule 22; that rule governs a repetition of the same element, and tavekh repeats nothing, so it would leave a lexical noun with no English against rule 2.
Suffix takes the pronoun it (rule 18).
Predicate construct noun takes men with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).
Nomen rectum takes of; great is the modifier the ASV supplies to complete the phrase, so the head stays on the lexeme-bearing stature (rules 19, 31).

review_notes: Both resumptive suffixes inside relative clauses are unrepresented, the written relative carrying the reference (rule 22).

betokah is rendered in it: the preposition and the construct noun tavekh share one unit on the single written in under rule 30, headed on tavekh, and the suffix takes it as the nomen rectum under rule 19. Corrected in chapter reconciliation from a reading that left tavekh unrepresented, which analysed this preposition-plus-construct pair unlike lipne at 13.22 and al odot at 13.24.
The ASV supplies no word for the object marker before the infinitive's object, and the anarthrous rendering of the rectum is what places each the (rules 16, 29).
